A timeline:

  • (2006) Intel first started releasing chips sporting the IME. The advertised purpose was to remotely control and monitor computers issued in a corporate setting. Primary security was through obscurity.
  • (2012) Some good Russian hackers (lel) released rather entertaining papers detailing the IME internals, culminating years of tracking down hidden documentation and old-fashioned probing. IME was found to have the watertightness of swiss cheese (almost certainly on purpose). Some groups began detailing and releasing attacks on the IME.
  • (2013-2017) Nobody gave a fuck, whilst security theater ('make sure you secure your OS! Use an Antivirus!', etc) continued on
  • (now) Intel: OMG Guis were so sorry we had no idea we will release a patch to fix these now trust us
